sentences.english: The brave soldier has a faithful dog.
The soldier's dog guards the small town.
The small boy sees the good dog.
For the boy praises the faithful dog.
And so the dog loves the boy.
The boy calls the dog and the soldier.
The dog and the soldier make for the boy.
The soldier sees and praises the boy.
The dog protects the boy and the soldier.

sentences.latin: Itaque mīles puerum et canem amat.
sentences.english: And so the soldier loves the boy and the dog.

sentences.latin: Vir agrum magnum prope oppidum habet.
sentences.english: The man has a large field near the town.

sentences.latin: Fēmina flōrēs pulchrōs in agrō videt.
sentences.english: The woman sees the beautiful flowers in the field.

sentences.latin: Itaque vir flōrēs pulchrōs fēminae dat.
sentences.english: And so the man gives the beautiful flowers to the woman.
The woman praises and loves the man.
The man gives the woman a new book.
The woman carries the book to the temple.
The man leads the woman to the temple.

sentences.latin: In templō vir et fēmina dōna dant.
sentences.english: In the temple, the man and woman give gifts.
The woman has her own small daughter.
The man gives a gift to the woman's daughter.
The small daughter loves the new gift.

sentences.latin: Cibus et vīnum in oppidō emuntur.
sentences.english: Food and wine are bought in the town.

sentences.latin: Cibus et vīnum ad mēnsam portantur.
sentences.english: Food and wine are carried to the table.

sentences.latin: Amīcus virī fēminam videt et virō invidet.
sentences.english: The man's friend sees the woman and envies the man.
The woman warns the man about the friend.
And so the man believes the woman.
But the friend makes for the woman's table.
The man sends the friend away from the table.
For the man warns the friend.

sentences.latin: Itaque vir fēminam et fīliam amat.
sentences.english: And so the man loves the woman and the daughter.

sentences.latin: Rēx sapiēns et rēgīna iūsta magnum rēgnum regunt.
sentences.english: The wise king and the just queen rule a great kingdom.

sentences.latin: Populus fidēlis magnae cīvitātis rēgem sapientem et rēgīnam iūstam amat.
sentences.english: The faithful people of the great state love the wise king and the just queen.

sentences.latin: Rēgīna praeclāra scēptrum vetus et corōnam pulchram habet.
sentences.english: The illustrious queen has an old scepter and a beautiful crown.

sentences.latin: Gravēs lēgēs omnium populōrum ā rēge sapientī servantur.
sentences.english: The weighty laws of all the peoples are preserved by the wise king.

sentences.latin: Itaque rēgīna praeclāra ā populō fidēlī et fēlīcī amātur.
sentences.english: And so the illustrious queen is loved by the faithful and happy people.
